items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the great stuff that was being done by Cannonball and Miles and Coltrane and Bird

ctx.x: You played late hours and I’d tear my em[bouchure]. I tell you, saxophone – that’s why I’m glad I played flute, because that saxophone, that embouchure, would almost kill me sometimes, playing those gigs, long hours. By playing those long hours, it took so much out of me. It was like doing manual labor. It wasn’t that gratifying, because at the time, when we were playing these gigs to satisfy these people with that superficial music, and at the same time we were aware of the great stuff that was being done by…
So it was more rhythm-and-blues rather than jazz? Or was it . . . ?
